0.0.n: Sets the time for the speaker’s update.

0.1.n: Adds a conversational pause and gently draws the listener in.

0.3.n: Emphasizes how recently the action was completed.

0.4.n: A shortened loanword referring to the plastic packaging.

0.5.n: Links シュリンク to 方 in a roundabout way of referring to the wrapping.

0.6.n: 方 softens the reference to シュリンク; it does not indicate a direction here.

0.7.n: Marks the wrapping as what was removed.

0.8.n: Past form of 取り除く, followed by ところ to show the action has just finished.

0.9.n: After a past verb, ところ expresses having just completed that action.

0.10.n: Makes the statement about the just-completed action polite.

0.11.n: Politely leads into the next point rather than expressing a strong contrast.

1.0.n: Introduces the first item the speaker will discuss.

1.1.n: An English loanword written in katakana.

1.2.n: Politely identifies the item being shown.

1.3.n: Gives the introduction a friendly, shared-observation tone.

2.0.n: Refers to the game being introduced.

2.1.n: Marks これ as the thing being described.

2.2.n: Part of an inserted ですね that gives the speaker a moment before continuing.

2.3.n: Helps hold the listener’s attention during the pause.

2.5.n: 用 after a number of people indicates how many people something is designed for.

2.6.n: Links 2人用 to the game description that follows.

2.7.n: 型 means type, making this a label for games where players face each other.

2.8.n: An English loanword naming the kind of game.

2.9.n: Connects the noun カードゲーム to the explanatory んです ending.

2.10.n: Short for の, adding a sense of explaining background information.

2.11.n: Makes the explanatory んです ending polite.

2.12.n: Keeps the explanation open and leads into further background.

3.0.n: Introduces the game’s background, which the speaker continues explaining in later lines.

3.1.n: Highlights 元々 as the frame for the explanation.

3.3.n: Refers to an earlier occasion involving the demo deck.

3.4.n: Links 前 to 体験デッキ, identifying the earlier demo deck.

3.5.n: Describes a deck intended to let people try the game.

3.6.n: A katakana loanword for a set of playing cards.

3.7.n: Links the demo deck to 時, referring to the occasion when it was discussed.

3.8.n: Refers to the earlier demo-deck presentation.

3.9.n: Marks 時 as the occasion when the introduction happened.

3.10.n: Shows that this information was presented on that earlier occasion too.

3.11.n: ご adds respect, while しました is the polite past form of する.

3.12.n: Connects the reminder of an earlier introduction to the explanation that follows.

4.1.n: The first part of the game’s name, Magic: The Gathering.

4.3.n: The remaining part of the game’s name, written in katakana.

4.5.n: Marks Magic: The Gathering as the comparison partner for 同じ.

4.6.n: Combines with ような to describe similarity rather than strict identity.

4.7.n: In 同じような, よう expresses resemblance to the game just named.

4.8.n: Lets 同じよう describe the noun phrase coming in the next line.

4.9.n: Part of an inserted ですね; the description continues afterward.

4.10.n: Adds a conversational pause before the speaker continues the comparison.

5.0.n: Describes a type of game where players compete against each other.

5.1.n: Links 対戦型 to トレーディングカードゲーム as its description.

5.2.n: A katakana term for games using collectible, tradable cards.

5.3.n: Links trading card games to the tradition expressed by 流れ.

5.4.n: Literally flow, used figuratively for a line of influence or development.

5.5.n: Marks 流れ as the object of 汲む.

5.6.n: Literally means draw water; 流れを汲む means inherit a tradition or influence.

5.7.n: An informal word referring to the game, described by the preceding phrase.

5.8.n: The connecting form used after a noun before ので.

5.9.n: Introduces the reason for the substantial rules described next.

6.0.n: Emphasizes the substantial amount of material in the rules.

6.1.n: An English loanword referring to how the game is played.

6.2.n: Links ルール to ほう, setting up the rules as the aspect under discussion.

6.3.n: Focuses attention on the rules aspect; no physical direction is intended.

6.4.n: Marks the rules as the topic of the statement.

6.5.n: This loanword refers to quantity of material, not sound level.

6.6.n: Marks ボリューム as what the rules have.

6.7.n: Polite form of ある; ボリュームがある describes something as substantial in size or content.

0.lit: Now, you know, I have just removed the shrink-wrap part, and…
0.tip: A past verb followed by ところです means the action has just been completed.

1.lit: First, it is the rulebook, you see.
1.tip: ですね makes identifying the item sound polite and conversational.

2.lit: This, you see, is a for-two-players competitive card game, and…
2.tip: なんです adds an explanatory tone after a noun.

3.lit: Originally, as for that, I also introduced it at the time of the previous demo deck, but…
3.tip: にも combines the occasion marker に with も to say the information was given on that occasion too.

4.lit: Like the same kind as Magic: The Gathering, you see…
4.tip: と同じような means similar to and connects to a noun, even across this spoken pause.

5.lit: Because it is one that draws on the tradition of competitive trading card games…
5.tip: 流れを汲む is an expression meaning to inherit a tradition or follow a line of influence.

6.lit: As for the rules side, there is quite a volume.
6.tip: ボリュームがあります means there is substantial content, not that something is loud.
